summary: Frontend testing of two new features. Feature 1 (BOM Explorer 'Run Cost Estimate' button) fully verified working as expected, including the known/escalated SAP-side error path. Feature 2 (Purchasing Plan 'Split Qty' supplier toggle) could NOT be verified end-to-end because Purchasing Plan generation itself is currently failing 100% of the time (5+ consecutive attempts, both via UI and direct API) due to an unhandled OMS read-timeout exception - a pre-existing gap in oms_client.py unrelated to this session's SAP semaphore fix.

critical.issue: Purchasing Plan generation fails 100% of the time in this session (5 consecutive attempts today, both via curl and UI, at 10:08, 10:09, 10:32, 10:37, 10:40) with error 'HTTPSConnectionPool(host=oms.radishtechnologies.com, port=443): Read timed out. (read timeout=30)'. Root cause: oms_client.py's _get() method (used by get_parts/get_monthly_demand/get_sales_plan, called via ThreadPoolExecutor across every OMS customer) does NOT wrap `requests.get(...)` in a try/except - only OMSClient._login() catches RequestException. So a single slow/timing-out customer call anywhere in the thread pool raises an uncaught requests.exceptions.ReadTimeout that propagates through executor.map() and crashes the entire job (status becomes 'failed'), instead of being logged+skipped like the sibling demand_planning_service.py does for the same OMS host (see its 'AMS: could not fetch OMS parts for X: Read timed out' WARNING logs which recover gracefully). This completely blocks the Purchasing Plan page and, by extension, this session's Feature 2 (Supplier Quota Split) could not be tested at all.

integration_issues.issue: Clicking Generate Purchasing Plan always ends in the 'Purchasing plan generation failed' error toast (see backend_issues.critical) after ~20-30s, for the default month. Could not reach the point of inspecting Suppliers column / Split Qty toggle at all.

action_items: Fix oms_client.py OMSClient._get(): wrap the `resp = requests.get(...)` calls in try/except requests.exceptions.RequestException and raise OMSError (mirroring _login()'s existing pattern), so that get_monthly_demand()/get_sales_plan()'s per-customer `fetch()` closures (which already catch OMSError) can skip a single failing customer instead of crashing the whole purchasing-plan job.

Once fixed, re-run Purchasing Plan generation and verify the Suppliers column 'Split Qty' toggle for SPC5WM (1 supplier, 60% quota) and/or SCR415WM/scr415wm (2 suppliers, 50%/55% quota) - confirmed quota_percent values are present in MongoDB part_suppliers collection right now, ready for the next testing pass.

Also worth checking: is oms.radishtechnologies.com itself under load / slow right now (root path returned 200 in 0.5s, so the host is up - only the deeper /api/ms/sales-monthly/parts calls for specific customers are timing out at 30s), separate infra item for main agent's awareness.

oms_client.py: _login() has requests.exceptions.RequestException handling but _get() (the far more frequently-called method, invoked once per customer per plan generation, often 50-100+ times via an 8-worker thread pool) has none - this asymmetry is the direct root cause of the current outage. Low-risk, contained fix.

rca_of_the_issue: Purchasing Plan generation depends on OMSClient.get_monthly_demand()/get_sales_plan(), which fan out one HTTP GET per OMS customer via an 8-worker ThreadPoolExecutor calling OMSClient._get(). _get() calls requests.get(...) with a 30s timeout but does NOT catch request exceptions (unlike _login(), which does and raises a clean OMSError). When any single customer's call read-times-out (observed repeatedly against oms.radishtechnologies.com's /api/ms/sales-monthly/parts endpoint - the host itself responds fine on other paths), the raw requests.exceptions.ReadTimeout escapes uncaught through get_parts() -> the fetch() closure in get_monthly_demand()/get_sales_plan() (which only catches OMSError, not generic RequestException) -> executor.map() -> the purchasing_plan job, killing the entire generation with 'failed' status. Confirmed via 5 consecutive real failures today (both curl-triggered and UI-triggered) all citing the identical error message, and via backend logs showing the sibling demand_planning_service.py module already has the correct defensive pattern (catches ReadTimeout and logs+skips per-customer) for the same OMS host, confirming this is a real, fixable code gap rather than a total OMS outage.
